_comment: Clean-arch port-placement gate policy (DATA, not code). ADR-0570. Productizes the defect class #116 exemplified: billing's `AccountingJournalStoragePort` storage-port trait was DEFINED in an in-memory ADAPTER crate, inverting the ports-in-core clean-arch convention proven by tenancy's TenantLifecycleStore and SCIM's UserStore/GroupStore (storage ports live in core/kernel crates; the adapter DEPENDS on core and IMPLEMENTS the port). This gate asserts that no `pub trait <Name>` whose name matches a storage/repository/port heuristic is DEFINED in a crate whose repo-relative path contains a forbidden layer-dir segment (`adapters`). The port belongs in a core/ports/kernel crate; the adapter must implement it, not own it. ALL repo-specifics are DATA here: a different repo adopts the gate by repointing port_name_suffixes / forbidden_layer_dirs / allowlist / the frozen baseline; the Rust engine hardcodes no oyatie crate name. The suffix set was calibrated by scanning the live corpus (2026-06-22): Store/Repository/Repo/StoragePort/Port catch the #116 class AND the existing tenant-rbac / session-store / secret-provider / kms-domain-repo storage ports, while behavioral adapter-internal traits (Authorizer/Backend/Adapter/Spawner/Observer/Provider/Actuator/Evaluator/Sink) are deliberately NOT matched so they never false-positive.
_allowlist_doc: Per-(crate, trait) carve-outs for a genuine false positive: an adapter-internal trait that is legitimately port-suffix-named but is NOT a relocatable storage port (e.g. an internal cursor/iterator). Each entry is {"crate": "<crate-dir-tail>", "trait": "<TraitName>", "reason": "..."}. Shrink-only: an allowlist entry matching no live finding becomes a PP-STALE-ALLOWLIST self-cleaning finding.

product_contract.born_advisory_enforce_no_regression: After #116 fixed billing, the live corpus still carries 5 pre-existing storage-port traits defined in adapter crates (the tenant-rbac/session/secret/kms ports — their relocation is separate per ADR-0570 scope discipline). They are captured in the FROZEN baseline (port-placement-baseline.json). The gate is born-ADVISORY against that baseline and enforces NO REGRESSION: a NEW port-suffix trait defined in an adapter crate (beyond the baseline) fails CLOSED. Baselined entries are ratchet-down only — relocating one is welcome and the gate self-cleans (a baseline entry matching no live finding becomes PP-STALE-BASELINE). The gate flips to fully BLOCKING when the baseline reaches 0.
product_contract.pack_shaped: forbidden_layer_dirs, port_name_suffixes, allowlist, min_expected_member_crates, and the baseline are DATA; the Rust kernel hardcodes no oyatie crate name. A different repo adopts the gate by repointing this policy + baseline.
product_contract.automation: AUTOMATED v1 = flag-with-precise-remediation: each finding names the exact trait, the adapter crate that wrongly defines it, and the sibling core/ports crate it should move to (inferred from the capability stem). A full auto-MOVE codemod (relocate the trait + its port-definitional types into core, rewrite the adapter to depend-and-implement) is a NOTED FOLLOW-UP, not this slice — a trait-relocation codemod is non-trivial and a design act.
product_contract.heuristic_soundness: The suffix set is an over-approximation in the SAFE direction for a born-advisory detector: it can only ever ADD a finding (which the baseline/allowlist absorb), never silently miss the #116 class. Behavioral adapter seams (Authorizer/Backend/Spawner/Observer/Provider/Actuator/Evaluator/Sink) carry none of the storage-port suffixes and are never flagged.

purpose: Clean-arch port-placement gate. A storage/repository/port trait must be DEFINED in a core/ports/kernel crate, not an adapter (the adapter implements it). Makes the #116 ports-in-adapter seam-mis-draw class impossible to ship new.
